title: One payment, two answers
subtitle: ORD-101 · sneakers · ₹4,999
voiceover: Imagine buying sneakers for four thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine rupees. Checkout confirms your payment.
Then My Orders says payment pending. You wonder whether to pay again.
This is an illustrative incident. Your payment succeeded; its history view is behind.

title: Commands change. Queries read.
subtitle: CQRS with separate stores
voiceover: A command changes information. A query reads it. CQRS separates those responsibilities.
Here we also use separate databases. The write database owns the order; history reads an optimized view.
That separation adds delay and operating costs. A single database is often enough.

title: Commit intent, then publish
subtitle: One local transaction · asynchronous Kafka delivery
voiceover: The provider outcome is verified outside PostgreSQL. One local transaction then saves paid version two and an outbox event.
A publisher sends that snapshot to Kafka using the order ID as its key.
Retries can publish duplicates. An outbox preserves intent; it does not make delivery instantaneous.

title: A delayed view is not a failed payment
subtitle: Payment confirmed. Your order history is synchronizing.
voiceover: The projection consumer is delayed. Kafka has the event, but the read database still holds pending version one.
Use verified confirmation to explain that history is synchronizing. Do not request another payment.
If payment itself is unknown, keep it under verification instead of promising success.

title: Accept newer. Reject stale. Ignore duplicates.
subtitle: Atomic PostgreSQL version guard
voiceover: The consumer recovers and applies paid version two. A separate replay path later republishes an older snapshot.
Kafka has not reordered its partition. An atomic database version guard rejects that older business version.
Identical duplicates change nothing. Conflicting payloads at the same version need investigation.

title: Recover the view. Preserve the payment.
subtitle: One order · one payment · history caught up
voiceover: Monitor pending outbox age, projection freshness and repair failures. Kafka lag alone cannot detect an unpublished event.
Reconciliation fetches the authoritative snapshot and applies the same guard. It never charges the shopper.
History now shows paid. Complete snapshots can skip versions; deltas may need gap recovery.
